title: God speaks through prophets, not birds
source_text: Τὸ δ᾿ ἀληθῶς θεῖον εἰς τὴν περὶ τῶν μελλόντων γνῶσιν οὔτε τοῖς ἀλόγοις χρῆται ζῴοις οὔτε τοῖς τυχοῦσι τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἀλλὰ ψυχαῖς ἀνθρώπων ἱερωτάταις καὶ καθαρωτάταις, ἅστινας θεοφορεῖ καὶ προφήτας ποιεῖ. διόπερ εἴ τι ἄλλο θαυμασίως εἴρηται ἐν τῷ Μωϋσέως νόμῳ, καὶ τὰ τοιαῦτα ἐν τοῖς τοιούτοις κατατακτέον· „οὐκ οἰωνιεῖσθε οὐδ᾿ ὀρνιθοσκοπήσετε,“ καὶ ἀλλαχοῦ· „τὰ γὰρ ἔθνη, οὓς κύριος ὁ θεός σου ἐξολοθρεύσει ἀπὸ προσώπου σου, οὗτοι κληδόνων καὶ μαντειῶν ἀκούσονται· σοὶ δὲ οὐχ οὕτως ἔδωκε κύριος ὁ θεός σου“· εἶθ᾿ ἑξῆς φησι· „προφήτην ἀναστήσει σοι κύριος ὁ θεός σου ἐκ τῶν ἀδελφῶν σου.“ βουληθεὶς δέ ποτε ὁ θεὸς δι᾿ οἰωνοσκόπου ἀποτρέψαι ἀπὸ τῆς οἰωνιστικῆς πεποίηκε πνεῦμα ἐν τῷ οἰωνοσκόπῳ εἰπεῖν· „οὐ γάρ ἐστιν οἰωνισμὸς ἐν Ἰακὼβ, οὐδὲ μαντεία ἐν Ἰσραήλ· κατὰ καιρὸν ῥηθήσεται τῷ Ἰακὼβ καὶ τῷ Ἰσραὴλ, τί ἐπιτελέσει ὁ θεός.“ ταῦτα δὴ γινώσκοντες ἡμεῖς καὶ τὰ τούτοις παραπλήσια τηρεῖν βουλόμεθα μυστικῶς εἰρημένην ἐντολὴν τήν· „πάσῃ φυλακῇ τήρει σὴν καρδίαν“· ἵνα μὴ ἐπιβῇ τι τῶν δαιμονίων τῷ ἡγεμονικῷ ἡμῶν, ἢ πνεῦμά τι τῶν ἐναντίων πρὸς ἃ βούλεται τρέψῃ τὸ φανταστικὸν ἡμῶν. εὐχόμεθα δὲ λάμψαι „ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ἡμῶν“ τὸν „φωτισμὸν τῆς γνώσεως τῆς δόξης τοῦ θεοῦ,“ ἐπιδημοῦντος ἡμῶν τῷ φανταστικῷ πνεύματος θεοῦ καὶ φαντάζοντος ἡμᾶς τὰ τοῦ θεοῦ· ἐπεὶ „ὅσοι πνεύματι θεοῦ ἄγονται, οὗτοι υἱοί εἰσι θεοῦ.“
pass_a_gloss: The truly divine (τὸ ἀληθῶς θεῖον) for the knowledge (γνῶσιν) about things to come uses (χρῆται) neither the irrational animals nor the chance (τυχοῦσι) of men, but the holiest (ἱερωτάταις) and purest (καθαρωτάταις) souls of men, which it God-bears/inspires (θεοφορεῖ) and makes prophets (προφήτας ποιεῖ). Wherefore if anything else has been wonderfully (θαυμασίως) said in the law (νόμῳ) of Moses, such things too must be ranked (κατατακτέον) among such: 'you shall not take bird-omens (οἰωνιεῖσθε) nor watch birds (ὀρνιθοσκοπήσετε)', and elsewhere: 'for the nations (ἔθνη), whom the Lord your God (κύριος ὁ θεός σου) will utterly destroy (ἐξολοθρεύσει) from before your face (προσώπου), these will hear omens (κληδόνων) and divinations (μαντειῶν); but to you not so did the Lord your God give (ἔδωκε)'; then next he says: 'a prophet will the Lord your God raise up (ἀναστήσει) for you from your brothers'. And God having once wished through an augur (οἰωνοσκόπου) to turn away (ἀποτρέψαι) from augury (οἰωνιστικῆς) has made a spirit (πνεῦμα) in the augur say: 'for there is no augury (οἰωνισμός) in Jacob, nor divination (μαντεία) in Israel; in season (κατὰ καιρόν) it will be said to Jacob and to Israel what God will accomplish (ἐπιτελέσει)'. Knowing these things then, and things close to them, we wish to keep (τηρεῖν) the commandment (ἐντολήν) spoken mystically (μυστικῶς): 'with all guarding (φυλακῇ) keep your heart (καρδίαν)'; that none of the demonic [powers] (δαιμονίων) may step upon (ἐπιβῇ) our ruling part (ἡγεμονικῷ), or some spirit of the opposing [powers] (ἐναντίων) may turn our imaginative faculty (φανταστικόν) to what it wishes. And we pray (εὐχόμεθα) that there shine (λάμψαι) 'in our hearts' the 'illumination of the knowledge of the glory of God', the Spirit of God sojourning in our imaginative faculty and imaging to us the things of God; since 'as many as are led by the Spirit of God, these are sons of God'.
pass_b_english: What is truly divine does not use irrational animals, nor just any men, for the knowledge of the future, but the holiest and purest souls of men, which it fills with God and makes prophets (Wisdom of Solomon 7:27). Therefore, if anything else in the law of Moses is wonderfully said, sayings like these must also be counted among them: “You shall not practise augury, nor watch birds” (Leviticus 19:26); and elsewhere: “For the nations, whom the Lord your God will destroy from before you, will listen to omens and divinations; but to you the Lord your God has not granted it so” (Deuteronomy 18:14); and then, next, he says: “The Lord your God will raise up for you a prophet from among your brothers” (Deuteronomy 18:15).

And once, when God wished to turn people away from augury through an augur, He caused a spirit in the augur to say: “For there is no augury in Jacob, nor divination in Israel; in due time it will be told to Jacob and to Israel what God will accomplish” (Numbers 23:23).

Knowing these things, and others like them, we wish to keep the commandment spoken in a mystical sense: “Keep your heart with all watchfulness” (Proverbs 4:23), so that none of the demons may set foot on our ruling faculty, and no spirit of the opposing powers may turn our imagination to what it wishes. And we pray that “the light of the knowledge of the glory of God” may shine “in our hearts” (2 Corinthians 4:6), while the Spirit of God dwells in our imagination and shapes in us images of the things of God; since “all who are led by the Spirit of God, these are sons of God” (Romans 8:14).

choices.choice: 'nor any chance men' -> 'nor just any men' (τοῖς τυχοῦσι; stiff calque)
'spoken in a mystery' -> 'spoken in a mystical sense' (μυστικῶς)

Scripture re-checked against LXX: Leviticus 19:26, Deuteronomy 18:14 (with 18:12 blended), 18:15, Numbers 23:23, Proverbs 4:23, 2 Corinthians 4:6, Romans 8:14 all say what is quoted; Wisdom 7:27 kept as a probable allusion (holy souls made prophets)

Leviticus 19:26 LXX οὐκ οἰωνιεῖσθε οὐδὲ ὀρνιθοσκοπήσεσθε, matches. Deuteronomy 18:14 LXX reads 'the nations which you are dispossessing'; Origen's 'whom the Lord your God will destroy from before you' draws on 18:12 ('the Lord will destroy them from before you'), so the quotation blends 18:12 and 18:14; cited to 18:14, where the main clause stands. Deuteronomy 18:15 matches. Numbers 23:23 is Balaam's oracle (Balaam the augur), wording matches the LXX. πεποίηκε πνεῦμα ἐν τῷ οἰωνοσκόπῳ εἰπεῖν is rendered 'caused a spirit in the augur to say'; Numbers 24:2 says 'the Spirit of God came upon him', but Origen's anarthrous πνεῦμα is left as 'a spirit' rather than capitalised. Proverbs 4:23 LXX πάσῃ φυλακῇ τήρει σὴν καρδίαν, matches. 2 Corinthians 4:6 (λάμψαι ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ἡμῶν πρὸς φωτισμὸν τῆς γνώσεως τῆς δόξης τοῦ θεοῦ), quoted in part; φωτισμός rendered 'light'. Romans 8:14 matches. 'Souls… which it fills with God and makes prophets' is a probable but not certain allusion to Wisdom 7:27 (wisdom 'passing into holy souls makes them friends of God and prophets'); cited inline, flagged here as an allusion. θεοφορεῖ rendered 'fills with God'. τὸ ἡγεμονικόν = the soul's ruling faculty (Stoic term); τὸ φανταστικόν = the faculty that forms images, rendered 'imagination'; φαντάζοντος ἡμᾶς τὰ τοῦ θεοῦ rendered 'shapes in us images of the things of God'. τῶν ἐναντίων rendered 'the opposing powers' (Origen's usual term for hostile spirits).
